info.bio:
Hanoi Rocks es un grupo de rock de Finlandia considerada como una de las más importantes influencias en el Glam Metal.

La época de más éxito de Hanoi Rocks fue a principio de los años 80. Musicalmente la banda esta influenciada por grupos como New York Dolls, The Stooges y los Rolling Stones. Su música fusiona elementos del blues, punk, heavy metal, garage rock y glam rock así como los principios fundamentales del Rock N' Roll al estilo Chuck Berry o Little Richard.

scenes.name: Revival psicodélico y garage de los ochenta
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El revival más persistente de los ochenta y noventa. En Los Ángeles, el «Paisley Underground»: Rain Parade, Three O'Clock, Dream Syndicate (síntesis de Dylan y la Velvet), Savage Republic, True West, Opal. En la Costa Este, los imitadores fetichistas (Lyres, Fuzztones, Chesterfield Kings) y bandas creativas (Das Damen, Plasticland, Eleventh Dream Day). El garage más crudo: Honeymoon Killers, Gibson Bros, Gories, Original Sins, God Bullies, Pandoras. La psicodelia libre de jams: Crystallized Movements, Magic Hour, Vocokesh, Sun City Girls, Black Sun Ensemble, Helios Creed. En Australia, Celibate Rifles, Died Pretty, Hoodoo Gurus, Beasts Of Bourbon, Scientists, Feedtime, Crime And The City Solution; en Europa, Hanoi Rocks, Echo & The Bunnymen, Teardrop Explodes, Bevis Frond, Legendary Pink Dots, The The y Love And Rockets.

mentions.text: …Waits' cocktail lounge in hell. Euro-garage 1980-86 The only area in Europe that could compete with USA's and Australia's garage-rock was Sweden. Hanoi Rocks (1), in particular, deserve to be named next to the father founders of the genre. This Finnish equivalent of the New York Dolls evolved from the punkish callowness of Bangkok Shocks Saigon Shakes Hanoi Rocks (1981) to the catchy power-pop of Oriental Beat (1982) to the slick glam-metal of Back To Mystery City (1983). podcast.title: Death in Car Crash (1984)
podcast.body: In 1984, drummer Razzle died in a car crash while being driven by Mötley Crüe's Vince Neil. Neil, who was drunk and speeding in his 1972 Ford Pantera, lost control and collided with two other cars, with Razzle dying at the hospital. "Razzle died in hospital."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Most Dangerous Artists in Rock

xref.title: Vehicular Manslaughter of Razzle (1984)
xref.body: In 1984, Vince Neil and Razzle, the drummer for Hanoi Rocks, left a party in Neil's powerful 1972 Ford Pantera to get more alcohol. While driving 65 mph in a 25 mph zone, Neil hit a wet patch, crossed into oncoming traffic, and crashed into two cars. Razzle died in the hospital, and Neil suffered cuts and cracked ribs. "While going 65 in a 25 miles per hour zone, the Pantera hit a wet patch of pavement, it crossed over into the opposite lane and crashed into two cars traveling the other way."
